quote: Really? You never never got a call?
stewart_read: Rep responds to a service-failure complaint with disbelief rather than acknowledgment, delaying the actual fix.
alternative_hypothesis: Could read as active listening/surprise rather than dismissal, but it still doesn't move toward resolution.
coaching_implication: Lead with acknowledgment ('that's not okay, let's get you a time that sticks') before probing — faster de-escalation.

quote: Man, I'm so sorry about that. What I can do here
stewart_read: Direct apology plus immediate offer to fix converts the customer from frustrated to cooperative in one line.
coaching_implication: This is the right move — do it on first touch of the complaint, not the second.

quote: What's your schedule looking like over the next couple of days?
stewart_read: Rep skips interest question, homeowner verify, bill, and roof entirely and goes straight to rebooking — reasonable given this is clearly a re-contact of an existing lead with a design already built, not a fresh qualify.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be a cut-corner truncation rather than context-justified, but the verified events show this is a repeat-touch call referencing a design already made, which supports the compression.
coaching_implication: None needed if this is confirmed a recycled/repeat lead; flag for lead-type metadata confirmation.

quote: Or I see we also have your fiance's number as well. No. This number would be best.
stewart_read: Rep surfaces a co-owner/fiance number but the customer directs contact to his own number only; rep does not confirm whether the fiance will be present on the appointment itself.
alternative_hypothesis: This may just be a contact-number preference, not a decision-maker exclusion — the fiance may not be on title, unclear from the call.
coaching_implication: Ask directly whether fiance should be included on the appointment call, not just which number to dial.

stewart_read: Customer accepts a time but button-up is incomplete — no explicit 'is that fair' handshake and no no-driving/computer instruction given.
coaching_implication: Add the fairness handshake and sit-down/no-driving line even on short rebooking calls to protect show rate.

quote: Just make sure you have access to your email at that time as well since we'll send you some details that way. Does that work?
stewart_read: Rep confirms email access but never states the appointment is a phone call with a locked hour block or the standard no-driving instruction.
coaching_implication: Close with the full button-up template, not a partial recap, to reduce no-show risk.
